questions.explanation: If the unequal side has length b, then b > (43 − b)/2 and b < 43 − b. Thus 43/3 < b < 43/2. Because 43 − b must be even, b can be 15, 17, 19, or 21.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, point D is on side AB and point E is on side AC. The segments BE and CD cross inside the triangle. If AD = 6, DB = 9, and AE = 5, what value of EC makes angle ADC equal in measure to angle AEB?
questions.explanation: The equal angles at D and E and the common angle at A make triangles ADC and AEB similar, with D corresponding to E. Hence 6/5 = AC/15, making AC = 18 and EC = 18 − 5.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has vertices A, B, C, and D in order, and diagonal AC lies inside it. The angles in triangle ABC at A, B, and C are x°, 2x°, and 3x°, respectively. The angles in triangle ADC at A, D, and C are 2y°, 3y°, and 4y°, respectively. How many degrees greater is the quadrilateral’s interior angle at C than its interior angle at A?
questions.explanation: The triangle sums give x = 30 and y = 20. At C the two pieces sum to 90° + 80° = 170°, and at A they sum to 30° + 40° = 70°.

questions.question: On a flat map, three streets are represented by lines p, q, and r. Line p has equation y = 2x + 1, line q has equation y = 2x − 9, and line r passes through (−1, 4) and (7, 0). How far apart are the two points where line r crosses lines p and q?
questions.explanation: Line r has slope −1/2 and intersects p at (1, 3) and q at (5, 1). The distance is √(4² + 2²) = 2√5.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, angle A measures 6° less than twice angle B. Extend side AB past B to a point D. If angle CBD measures three times angle C, what is the measure of angle A, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Write b and c for the measures of angles B and C. Supplementary angles give b + 3c = 180, and the triangle gives 3b + c = 186. Solving gives b = 47.25, so angle A is 88.5.

questions.question: A groundskeeper measures three sides of a triangular garden bed to see whether one corner is a right angle. Which set of side lengths, in meters, confirms that the bed has a right angle?
questions.explanation: The squares of the two shorter lengths sum to the square of the longest: 12² + 35² = 37².

questions.question: In right triangle JKL, K is the right angle. The hypotenuse JL is 41 units long, and the leg KL is 40 units long. For how many of the two acute angles is the sine greater than 1/2?
questions.explanation: Angle J has sine 40/41. The other leg has length √(41² − 40²) = 9, so angle L has sine 9/41.

questions.question: A square stage has a diagonal of 14√2 meters. What is the distance around the stage, in meters?
questions.explanation: The diagonal and two edges form a 45°-45°-90° triangle. Each edge is 14√2 ÷ √2 = 14 meters, so the perimeter is 56.

questions.question: Three squares are built outward on the three sides of a right triangle, each using one side of the triangle as a full edge. The two squares on the legs have areas 16 and 72 square centimeters. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the square on the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: The Pythagorean theorem says that the square on the hypotenuse has area equal to the sum of the other two areas.

questions.question: A straight zip line makes a 22° angle with the horizontal. In a vertical cross section through the zip line, what is the measure of the acute angle between the line and a vertical post?
questions.explanation: Horizontal and vertical directions are perpendicular, so the acute angles with the zip line add to 90°.

questions.question: Seen from the side, a brace, a wall, and the floor form a right triangle. The brace meets the floor 4 meters from the wall and meets the wall 3 meters above the floor. The brace makes an acute angle θ with the wall. Which equation is true?

options.text: tan θ = 3/4
sin θ = 3/5
cos θ = 4/5
tan θ = 4/3

questions.explanation: Relative to the angle at the wall, the 4-meter floor segment is opposite and the 3-meter wall segment is adjacent.

questions.question: A ship’s mast is 18 meters tall. From an eye-level point on a nearby dock, the top of the mast is at an angle of elevation of 26°. The eye-level point is 2 meters above the foot of the mast. Which expression gives the horizontal distance, in meters, from the dock observation point to the mast?
questions.explanation: The vertical difference is 18 − 2 = 16 meters. Tangent is vertical difference divided by horizontal distance, so solve for the distance.

questions.question: A triangular support has perpendicular legs of lengths 12 and x, where x is positive. Its hypotenuse is exactly 6 units longer than the leg of length x. What is x?
questions.explanation: Set 12² + x² = (x + 6)². Cancel x² and solve 144 = 12x + 36 to get x = 9.

questions.question: A circular sign is fixed to the end of a 10-foot rigid arm that pivots at ground level. The end of the arm is raised by changing the angle the arm makes with level ground from 30° to 60°. By how many feet does the end of the arm rise?
questions.explanation: The end’s height is 10 sin 30° before the move and 10 sin 60° after it. Subtract 5 from 5√3.

questions.question: Two right triangles have congruent hypotenuses. A leg of the first triangle is 3/5 of its hypotenuse, and a leg of the second is 7/10 of its hypotenuse. Which statement about the acute angles opposite these legs is true?

options.text: The angle in the first triangle is greater.
The two angles have equal measures.
The angle in the second triangle is greater.
The second angle is 10° greater.

questions.explanation: The sines are 0.6 and 0.7. Sine increases as an acute angle increases, so the second triangle has the larger angle.

questions.question: A square practice field has sides 50 meters long. A runner goes in a straight line from one corner to the midpoint of a side that does not touch that corner. The runner then follows that side to one of its endpoints. Which expression gives the runner’s total distance, in meters?
questions.explanation: The straight segment has perpendicular components 50 and 25, making its length √(50² + 25²) = 25√5. The last segment is 25 meters.

questions.question: A straight cable runs inside a rectangular crate from one bottom corner to the farthest top corner. The inside floor is 20 inches long and 12 inches wide. The cable makes a 45° angle with its projection onto the floor. What is the length of the cable, in inches?
questions.explanation: The floor diagonal is √(20² + 12²) = 4√34. This is one leg of a 45°-45°-90° triangle whose hypotenuse is the cable, so multiply by √2.

questions.question: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 25. The altitude drawn from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse divides the hypotenuse into two segments. The shorter leg of the triangle has length 10. What is the length of the shorter of the two segments on the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: The smaller right triangle adjacent to the shorter leg is similar to the original. The ratio of the shorter hypotenuse segment to 10 equals 10/25, so the segment has length 4.

questions.question: Two points on level ground are on the same side of a vertical tower and in a straight line with its base. The points are 24 meters apart. From the farther point, the tangent of the angle of elevation to the top is 1/3. From the nearer point, the tangent is 3/5. How tall is the tower, in meters?
questions.explanation: For a tower of height h, the farther point is 3h meters away and the nearer one is 5h/3 meters away. Their difference is 24, so h = 18.

questions.question: For an acute angle θ in a right triangle, sin θ = 2 cos θ. What is the value of sin θ + cos θ?
questions.explanation: The opposite leg is twice the adjacent leg. Taking them as 2 and 1 gives hypotenuse √5, so the sum is 3/√5 = 3√5/5.

questions.question: A trapezoid has a 32-centimeter horizontal lower base and a 12-centimeter horizontal upper base. The left and right sides both slope inward going up from the lower base. The tangents of the acute angles the lower base makes with the left and right sides are 2/3 and 4, respectively. What is the height of the trapezoid, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: For height h, the left and right sides move inward by 3h/2 and h/4. These distances sum to 32 − 12 = 20. Thus 7h/4 = 20 and h = 80/7.

questions.question: A circular game board is centered at O. Three points on its edge are A, B, and C. Points A and B are on opposite sides of O and lie on the same straight line through O. Which expression must equal the length of segment AB?

options.text: OC/2
OC
2 × OC
π × OC

questions.explanation: AB is a diameter and OC is a radius. The diameter is twice the radius.

questions.question: The edge of a circular sign is marked with three points P, Q, and R, in that order clockwise. The clockwise arc from P to Q measures 112°, and the clockwise arc from Q to R measures 97°. What is the degree measure of the clockwise arc from R back to P?
questions.explanation: The three consecutive arcs complete the circle. The remaining measure is 360° − 112° − 97° = 151°.

questions.question: A robot starts at a marked point on a circular track that is 96 meters long. It travels 132 meters clockwise along the track without stopping or reversing. When it stops, how many meters of clockwise travel remain before it next reaches the marked point?
questions.explanation: The robot completes one lap and travels 36 more meters. It then has 96 − 36 = 60 meters left.

questions.question: Two concentric circles are drawn around the same point. The inner circle has radius 7 centimeters, and the outer circle has radius 11 centimeters. How many centimeters longer is the circumference of the outer circle than that of the inner circle?

options.text: 8π
4π

questions.explanation: The circumferences are 22π and 14π. Their difference is 8π.

questions.question: A circle centered at (2, −1) passes through (2, 4). Which other point is on this same circle?
questions.explanation: The given point is 5 units from the center, as is (−3, −1), which is 5 units directly to its left.

questions.question: A line is tangent to a circle centered at (−2, 1) at the point (4, 4). Which equation represents the tangent line?
questions.explanation: The radius to (4, 4) has slope 3/6 = 1/2. The perpendicular tangent has slope −2 and passes through (4, 4).

questions.question: Two different circles have radii 5 centimeters and 8 centimeters. A central angle of 144° in the smaller circle cuts off an arc. What central angle, in degrees, cuts off an arc of the same length in the larger circle?
questions.explanation: Equal arc lengths give equal products of radius and angle when both angles use the same unit. The larger circle’s angle is 5 × 144 ÷ 8 = 90°.

questions.question: The four vertices A, B, C, and D of a convex quadrilateral lie on a circle in that order. The interior angles at A and C measure (4x + 8)° and (2x + 4)°, respectively. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: The arcs intercepted by angles A and C together make the entire circle. Each inscribed angle is half its arc’s measure, so 6x + 12 = 180.

questions.question: A road is represented by the horizontal line y = 6. A circular service area centered at (3, 2) just touches the road. Which point is strictly inside the service area?
questions.explanation: The radius is the center’s perpendicular distance to the road, 4. For (5, 5) the squared distance is 2² + 3² = 13, less than 16.

questions.question: Points P and Q are the ends of a diameter of a circle. Point R is on the circle and is different from P and Q. The area of triangle PRQ is 30 square units, and PR = 5. What is RQ?
questions.explanation: An inscribed angle that intercepts a diameter is a right angle. The area is therefore (PR × RQ)/2, so RQ = 60/5.

questions.question: A circular track of radius 6 meters is divided by regularly spaced markers into 12 arcs of equal length. Instead of following the outer edge, a runner cuts straight across from one marker to the marker two positions clockwise. How long is that straight shortcut?

options.text: 2π meters
6 meters
3 meters
6√3 meters

questions.explanation: Two of the 12 marker intervals form a 60° central angle. The two radii and the shortcut form an equilateral triangle.

questions.question: A sprinkler centered at (0, 0) can reach any point within 10 meters, including points exactly 10 meters away. A planting row follows the line 3x + 4y = 30, with coordinates measured in meters. What length of the row, in meters, can the sprinkler reach?
questions.explanation: The closest point on the row is 30/√(3² + 4²) = 6 meters from the center. It bisects the reachable chord, whose half-length is √(10² − 6²) = 8.

questions.question: A stage canopy has the shape of a ring sector: it lies between two concentric arcs of radii 5 meters and 9 meters and between the same two radii directions. The longer arc along the outer edge of the canopy is 6π meters long. What is the area of the canopy, in square meters?
questions.explanation: The outer edge is 6π out of the full 18π circumference, so the canopy is one-third of the ring. Its area is π(9² − 5²)/3.

questions.question: A fixed circle centered at (0, 0) has radius 7. A second circle centered at (10, 0) has positive radius r. Which range of r gives exactly two distinct points common to both circles?
questions.explanation: At r = 3 the circles touch externally, and at r = 17 they touch internally. The boundaries cross twice only between those values.

questions.question: Points A, B, and C lie on a circle with center O, and O lies inside triangle ABC. The measure of angle OAB is 24°, and the measure of angle OBC is 31°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the minor arc from A to C?
questions.explanation: Triangles AOB and BOC are isosceles because the sides from O are radii. Their angles at O are 180° − 2(24°) = 132° and 180° − 2(31°) = 118°. The remaining central angle is 360° − 132° − 118° = 110°.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a square of side length 10. A smaller circle is placed inside one corner of the square, tangent to both sides that meet at that corner and externally tangent to the larger circle. What is the radius of the smaller circle?
questions.explanation: The centers lie on the corner diagonal at perpendicular distances 5 and r from each side. Their separation is (5 − r)√2, which equals 5 + r. Solving gives r = 15 − 10√2.
